correctness.rationale: The order complex of \(A_1\oplus\cdots\oplus A_h\) is the join of the discrete levels, so \(H_{h-1}\cong\bigotimes_i\ker(\varepsilon_i)\). Projecting an order-preserving self-map to nondegenerate top simplices gives a tensor product of level maps \(g_i\). If the top action is nonzero, every \(g_i\) is nonzero on the augmentation kernel; the chain-map condition forces the indicator of points mapped back into level \(i\) to be constant, hence identically one. Thus every level is preserved. For a level map with image size \(s_i\), the induced augmentation-kernel image has rank \(s_i-1\), yielding rank \(\prod_i(s_i-1)\). Nonzero action is therefore equivalent to levelwise nonconstancy, and maximal rank to levelwise bijectivity. The counting formula \(\prod_i(r_i^{r_i}-r_i)\) follows independently level by level. The bundled exact enumeration agrees in the listed small weak orders.

value.rationale: Finite weak orders and joins of discrete sets are natural finite topological models. The theorem gives a complete structural classification of which self-maps are detected by top homology, the exact rank of every nonzero action, and the exact count of such maps. This is a reusable map-level invariant, not merely a finite census.
